clue.text: Apparently no socialists and I agree

definitions.meaning: taken literally, a group with no lefts at all is entirely right-wing
a phrase of assent, like 'fine by me' or 'OK'

explanation.surface: Someone notes that there seem to be no socialists present and signals approval.
explanation.walkthrough: Socialists are on the political left, so a gathering with none of them would read as one made up of the right only.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a common idiom of assent, said when accepting a proposal.

clue.text: Sack remained unused

definitions.meaning: to sack a town is to plunder and ravage it
land that stayed uncultivated is said to have lain in that idle state, past tense of the phrase

explanation.surface: An empty bag that was never put to use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sack' looks like a noun for a bag, but it is the verb meaning to plunder a town; the second reading uses lay as the past of lie.
explanation.definitionFit: To sack a city is to plunder and devastate it; idle ground left untilled was also said to do this.

clue.text: All set to scan far side of galaxy

parts.note: to scan a text is to read it

indicators.note: the far side of a word is its final letter, here of galaxy

explanation.surface: An astronomer is prepared to survey the remote edge of a galaxy.
explanation.definitionFit: Being all set means being prepared to start, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Pass ring successfully

definitions.meaning: to pass an exam or test, to come through it
to make a telephone call that connects with the person called

explanation.surface: An athlete passes a ring in a gymnastics or ball game without mishap.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to succeed in a test and to reach someone by telephone.

clue.text: Non-alcoholic drink brewed in East

indicators.note: brewing works ingredients together, so the letters of the words in East are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A soft drink such as tea is made in the Orient.
explanation.definitionFit: A herbal infusion, served hot like tea, which contains no alcohol.

clue.text: Fox starts to be evasive, catching birds

indicators.note: one piece catches another by holding it inside
the starts of words are their first letters, here of be and evasive

parts.note: emus are large flightless Australian birds

explanation.surface: A fox avoids capture while it grabs some birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fox' looks like the animal of the surface, but it is the verb meaning to baffle.
explanation.definitionFit: To fox someone is to puzzle or confuse them, a synonym.

clue.text: 13 down

definitions.meaning: refers to the answer at 13 across, a verb meaning to squander money

explanation.walkthrough: To blue money is old British slang for spending it recklessly, which fits the verb at 13.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is slang for squandering cash and also an everyday word for feeling depressed.

clue.text: Commissioning soldier with regular girlfriend?

parts.note: a man is a private soldier, as in officers and men
someone dating is going out with a steady partner; the question mark admits the loose fit

explanation.surface: A soldier is posted to a new duty while also seeing a steady girlfriend.
explanation.definitionFit: Mandating something means formally ordering or authorising it, like commissioning a piece of work.

clue.text: I tested them at work to check the flow

indicators.note: the letters are set working in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An engineer has tested some devices on the job to monitor water flow.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to halt a rising trend, literally holding back the incoming sea.

clue.text: Ruler rejects any dubious packages from the East

indicators.note: in an across clue, reading from the east means reading right to left, backwards
the words package up the letters, which are concealed inside them

explanation.surface: A monarch refuses suspicious parcels that have come from the Orient.
explanation.definitionFit: A dynast is a hereditary ruler, a member of a ruling dynasty.

clue.text: 6 down note introduced to band (Queen)

indicators.note: the note goes inside the band

parts.note: a squad is a band of people working together
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, Queen Elizabeth

explanation.surface: A musical note is added to a band, and the band is Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the answer at 6 down, used in its slang sense of to spend recklessly.
explanation.definitionFit: To blue money is to waste it extravagantly, a synonym of the verb here.

clue.text: Toy to produce reedy note

parts.note: to play a note is to produce it on an instrument
a reedy voice or sound is thin and high
G is a musical note

explanation.surface: A child's toy can make a high, piping note.
explanation.definitionFit: A toy is an object for a child to play with, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Extra run accorded to the winners?

definitions.text: Extra run accorded to the winners?

parts.words: Extra run accorded to the winners?
parts.note: after a victory, the champions run one more circuit of the track or ground to celebrate with fans

explanation.walkthrough: 'Extra run' hints at a cricket extra, but the run here is a celebratory circuit.
explanation.definitionFit: A celebratory circuit by victors, taken purely to salute the crowd, is an additional run on top of the race.

clue.text: See 2
Designer briefly dipped into gold reserves for yarns we hear

indicators.note: one piece is dipped into another, going inside it

parts.note: AU is the chemical symbol for gold
to book a seat is to reserve it

indicators.note: shortened, losing its final letter

parts.note: Christian Dior was a French fashion designer

explanation.surface: A fashion designer briefly dips into a stash of gold for stories.
explanation.walkthrough: Dior is the French fashion house; 'reserves' is a verb here, not a noun for stores of gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Recorded readings of novels are stories one listens to rather than reads.

clue.text: No part in play for angel?

indicators.note: the letters are put in play, moving freely into a new order

explanation.surface: A would-be actor gets no role in a play and wonders about playing an angel.
explanation.walkthrough: In theatre an angel is a financial backer of a production, which suits the stage surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatrical angel is a financial backer or sponsor, which is what a supporter of the arts is.

clue.text: They said I must leave supply outside empty store now

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go around the other piece
read as supple-y, in a pliant way, so the remaining letters bend into a new order
the letter I has to depart from the words They said

parts.note: the letter I as written

indicators.note: an empty word keeps only its outer letters, here of store

explanation.surface: Someone was told they must leave and supply goods from outside a vacant shop now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must leave' takes I from THEY SAID to give THEYSAD; 'supply' rearranges that to THEDAYS, which 'outside' wraps around SE from 'empty store'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means at the present time, in modern times, which is what now means.

clue.text: Flat in a revolting state during function

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other, as an event sits within a period

parts.note: sine is a trigonometric function
people up in arms are in revolt, as in 'the town is up'

explanation.surface: A country in rebellion lies prostrate during some official ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying supine means lying flat on one's back.

clue.text: Take first flight from Liechtenstein border

parts.note: FL is the international vehicle registration code for Liechtenstein
an edge is a border or rim

explanation.surface: Someone flies out for the first time from the frontier of Liechtenstein.
explanation.definitionFit: A young bird fledges when it grows feathers and leaves the nest flying.

clue.text: Antelope shortened stride, there being nothing ahead

indicators.note: the nothing piece comes ahead of, before, the other

parts.note: nil means nothing, zero

indicators.note: cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: a gait is a manner of walking, a stride

explanation.surface: A running antelope shortens its stride, with nothing in front of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A large Indian antelope, the bluebuck, is known by this Hindi-derived name.

clue.text: Fellow departs after pinching Georgia's butt

indicators.note: the departs piece comes after the rest
the fellow pinches, gripping the other piece inside

parts.note: a don is a college fellow at Oxford or Cambridge
GE is the international code for the country Georgia
D is the timetable abbreviation for departs

explanation.surface: A man leaves after pinching someone called Georgia on the bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butt' looks like a backside in the surface, but it means a cigarette end.
explanation.definitionFit: A butt is the stub of a smoked cigarette, which in British slang has this name.

clue.text: Retired like Menuhin, unable to play on?

parts.note: Yehudi Menuhin was a violinist, and a violin is played with a bow
a batsman or player who is out can no longer continue playing

explanation.surface: A violinist like Menuhin stopped performing because he could no longer play.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave a role or contest gracefully is to withdraw from it, that is, to retire.

clue.text: Doctor in Bedford 27

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: A physician works in the town of Bedford.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the answer at 27 down, in its sense of not allowed. Bedford is an English county town.
explanation.definitionFit: Something out is barred or not permitted, as in 'smoking is out'.

clue.text: Stay and prosper, having refused Oscar

indicators.note: the piece has turned the letter away, so it is removed

parts.note: to do well is to prosper
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone stays on and thrives after turning down an Academy Award.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwell somewhere is to live or remain there, so stay is a synonym.

clue.text: Baby boomer's drug-inspired rapture?

indicators.note: the rapture breathes in, inspires, the drug, taking it inside

parts.note: joy is rapture or delight
E is short for ecstasy, the drug

explanation.surface: A member of the post-war generation had a drug-fuelled moment of bliss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Baby boomer' suggests the post-war generation, but a boomer is a large male kangaroo in Australia, and its baby has its own name.
explanation.definitionFit: A young kangaroo is called a joey, and a boomer is an adult male kangaroo.

clue.text: Sleeping partner with huge guts joining firm

indicators.note: the firm piece joins on to the rest

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm

indicators.note: the huge piece forms the partner's guts, sitting in the middle

parts.note: a mate is a partner
OS stands for outsize, a clothing size

explanation.surface: A sleeping partner with a big belly joins a business.
explanation.walkthrough: A sleeping partner is an investor in a firm who takes no active part, which colours the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Comatose describes someone deeply unconscious, used loosely of being fast asleep.

clue.text: Performing bears about to leave coastal state

indicators.note: the performing piece bears, carries, the others inside

parts.note: an actor who is on is performing on stage
re means about, concerning
to go is to leave

explanation.surface: Dancing bears are about to depart from a seaside region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Performing bears' looks like circus animals, or an anagram, but 'bears' is the containment.
explanation.definitionFit: Oregon is a US state with a Pacific coastline.

clue.text: See 21
Like pie made by chef initially out of practice?

indicators.note: the initial letter of the word chef

parts.note: rusty skills are out of practice from lack of use

explanation.surface: A pie made by a cook who has not baked for a while.
explanation.definitionFit: A pie has a pastry crust, so it can be described as having one.

clue.text: Miserable miss, on reflection, breaking engagement

indicators.note: the reflected piece breaks into the engagement, sitting inside it

parts.note: a date is an appointment or engagement

indicators.note: reflected in a mirror, the word is read backwards

parts.note: to miss is to lose, as with a chance

explanation.surface: An unhappy young woman, thinking it over, breaks off her engagement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'miss' looks like a young woman but is the verb meaning to lose.
explanation.definitionFit: Desolate means wretched and forlorn, a synonym of very unhappy.
